what_its_for: This medicine is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the urinary tract (including the kidneys) and infections in the belly area (intra-abdominal infections). It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It is only used for infections that are caused by bacteria that are hard to treat with other antibiotics.
how_to_take: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous) line directly into your vein. A healthcare provider will give you each dose in a hospital or clinic setting. The medicine drips slowly into your vein over about 1 hour each time. You will not be giving this medicine to yourself at home unless your doctor or nurse has specifically trained you to do so. Always follow the instructions given to you by your healthcare team.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your kidneys are working. A common adult dose is 1.5 grams (ceftolozane 1 gram plus tazobactam 0.5 gram) given every 8 hours. For some serious lung infections, a higher dose may be used. The full course of treatment usually lasts 4 to 14 days depending on your infection. Do not stop treatment early even if you feel better, as this can allow the infection to come back or become harder to treat.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic, it is unlikely that you will miss a dose. If you are receiving this medicine at home through a home infusion service and you miss a scheduled dose, contact your home health nurse or doctor right away for instructions. Do not try to double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: This medicine will be stored and handled by your healthcare team or home infusion pharmacy. If you are receiving it at home, keep the medicine refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Do not freeze it. Once the bag has been prepared and mixed, it should be used within the time frame your pharmacist tells you. Keep it out of direct sunlight and away from children. Do not use the medicine if it looks cloudy, has particles in it, or if the bag or container is damaged.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines you are taking, including vitamins, supplements, and herbal products, before starting this antibiotic. Avoid taking other antibiotics or medicines that are not approved by your doctor while on this treatment. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early. If you develop diarrhea during or after treatment, avoid taking anti-diarrhea medicines without talking to your doctor first, as diarrhea can sometimes be a sign of a serious gut infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience any of the following: a severe allergic reaction such as skin rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe or watery diarrhea, diarrhea with blood or mucus, or stomach cramps (this could be a sign of a serious bowel infection called C. diff); seizures or shaking; unusual bruising or bleeding; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dark urine; or signs that your infection is getting worse such as increasing fever, chills, or pain. Also call your doctor if you notice any redness, swelling, or pain at your IV site.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is very important to finish the full course of antibiotics your doctor prescribed even if you feel well. The infection may not be fully cleared if you stop early. Your doctor may order lab tests or imaging during treatment to check that the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor will adjust your dose to keep the medicine safe for you. Blood tests to check kidney function may be done during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more likely to have kidney problems, so your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known, so your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits with you. Children: This medicine may be used in children in certain situations; the dose will be based on the child's weight and will be determined by the doctor. Patients with allergies to penicillin or cephalosporins: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin, cephalosporins, or any other antibiotic, as you may have a higher chance of reacting to this medicine.
